LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
  <decision>SAFE</decision>
  <details>
    Analysis: The PKGBUILD starts by assigning variables such as pkgname, pkgver, _tag, pkgdesc, arch, url, license, depends, makedepends, checkdepends, optdepends, options, backup, source, sha256sums. It then defines four functions: prepare, build, check, package. When running makepkg --printsrcinfo, only the top-level code is executed, which merely reads these variables and builds the string for the source variable. No command substitution, no eval, no base64, no curl or wget calls appear. The source variable points to a URL under the project's releases directory, which is the expected upstream artifact for the source tarball; downloading occurs later during the build phase, not at sourcing time. Therefore sourcing the PKGBUILD does not launch any payload or exfiltrate data. Mutable branch handling via _tag is normal for AUR packages and does not introduce a supply chain attack at this stage.
  </details>
  <evidence>
  </evidence>
  <summary>Top-level only variable setup; no commands; safe.</summary>
</security_assessment>
